headline: Claims the spacetime Penrose inequality: a black hole's enclosing area caps how small the total mass can be.
scope: Asymptotically flat and anti-de Sitter initial data in general relativity, with trapped boundaries, charge or rotation, across thirteen companion papers.
plain: The Penrose inequality says a spacetime holding a black hole must carry at least a set mass, fixed by the horizon's area. It was known for the special case where the data has no time motion, but the general spacetime case was open. Thirteen papers claim to prove it in the general setting, plus versions with charge, rotation and a negative cosmological constant. Lean checks only one supporting construction and a family of equality examples.
doesNot: This does not prove cosmic censorship, and Lean does not check the main inequality, the charged or rotating versions, or the rigidity theorems.
origin: This result comes from an unreleased OpenAI model, published in the openai/math release on 6 October 2026.

scorecard.firstStepBy: Roger Penrose, null-shell argument linking mass, horizon area and cosmic censorship
scorecard.significanceWhy: The spacetime Penrose inequality is a long-standing central conjecture of mathematical general relativity.

explanation:
Take the simplest black hole, the Schwarzschild solution of Einstein's equations. Use units where the speed of light and the gravity constant are 1. A black hole of mass m = 1 then has a horizon of radius 2m = 2. Its area is 4π × 2², which is 16π, about 50.27. In everyday units, a black hole as heavy as the Sun has a horizon radius near 2.95 km. Its area is near 110 square km. Turn this around. If a horizon has area A, the mass should be at least the square root of A/(16π). For A = 16π, that gives 1, so Schwarzschild sits exactly on the line.

Penrose's null-shell argument made this comparison concrete[1]. It came from a test of cosmic censorship, the idea that collapse ends in a black hole hidden by a horizon. To state it as a theorem, you describe one moment of time by initial data. This is a space, its metric (the rule for distances), and its second fundamental form (how the slice bends inside spacetime). The mass is the ADM mass, read off far away. The horizon is replaced by a trapped boundary, a surface where outgoing light cannot spread out.

The case with zero bending was settled long ago. Bray's conformal flow proves the sharp bound for the total area of a possibly disconnected horizon[2]. With general bending, nonzero second fundamental form, the method breaks. Neither scalar curvature nor the boundary mean curvature has the required Riemannian sign[3]. That sign problem is the main obstacle.

The papers claim that the enclosing-area form of the spacetime Penrose conjecture holds in their class of data[4]. The area used is the smallest area of any surface that encloses the boundary. They do not assume the boundary is outermost or area-minimizing[5]. With electric and magnetic charge Q, they claim m ≥ Q and r_A ≤ m + √(m² − Q²), where r_A is the enclosing-area radius[6]. For m = 1 and Q = 0.6, the radius is at most 1.8, so the area is at most about 40.7. A rotating version, the Kerr–Newman Penrose inequality, is also claimed[7]. One paper builds examples that break that rotating version when the angular momentum omits its electromagnetic part[8]. Another set claims versions for a negative cosmological constant, the anti-de Sitter setting[9]. For equality cases, the papers claim the data must be a slice of a Schwarzschild–Tangherlini exterior[10].

How sure is this? Lean, a computer proof checker, covers only one supporting step. It formalizes replacing one type of curved end by a flat end while keeping energy and area under control. It also checks that Schwarzschild data gives equality at every positive mass. The main inequality, the charged, rotating and anti-de Sitter versions, and the equality theorems rest on thirteen long papers. No specialist review of them has been published.
hypeCheck: Major if it holds. Lean covers one end-replacement step and the Schwarzschild equality examples only; the main inequalities rest on thirteen long papers with no published specialist review.

glossary.meaning: The claim that total mass is at least the square root of the horizon area divided by 16π, in units where light speed and the gravity constant are 1.
A snapshot of spacetime at one moment: a space with a distance rule (metric) and a record of how it bends in time (second fundamental form).
The total mass of a spacetime, measured from the shape of space very far away.
A closed surface where light sent outward does not spread out, the sign of a black hole.
The smallest area of any surface that separates the trapped boundary from infinity.
The simplest black hole: no spin, no charge, perfectly round. It is the equality case.
A spacetime with a negative cosmological constant, so space curves like a saddle at large distances.

claims.text: Bray's conformal flow proved the sharp Riemannian bound for the total area of a possibly disconnected horizon.
claims.sourceLine: Bray's conformal flow changes the metric, preserving the horizon area and making mass nonincreasing, and proves the sharp bound for the total area of a possibly disconnected horizon
claims.sourceQuote: Bray's conformal flow changes the metric, preserving the horizon area and making mass nonincreasing, and proves the sharp bound for the total area of a possibly disconnected horizon \cite{Bray2001}.

claims.sourceLine: Thus the enclosing-area form of the spacetime Penrose conjecture holds in this class.
claims.sourceQuote: Thus the enclosing-area form of the spacetime Penrose conjecture holds in this class.

claims.text: For charged data the bound is m ≥ Q and r_A ≤ m + √(m² − Q²).
claims.sourceQuote: Writing $m$ for invariant ADM mass, $Q$ for total charge magnitude, and $r_A$ for the minimum-enclosing-area radius, the bound is $m\ge Q$ and $r_A\le m+\sqrt{m^2-Q^2}$.

claims.text: The sharp Kerr–Newman Penrose inequality is claimed for axisymmetric electrovacuum exteriors.
claims.sourceLine: We prove the sharp Kerr--Newman Penrose inequality
claims.sourceQuote: We prove the sharp Kerr--Newman Penrose inequality \[ m^2\ge \frac{A}{16\pi}+\frac{Q^2}{2} +\frac{\pi(Q^4+4J^2)}{A}. \]

claims.text: Smooth axisymmetric exteriors violate the Kerr–Newman inequality when J is the bare gravitational ADM angular momentum.
claims.sourceLine: violate the Kerr--Newman Penrose inequality when \(J\) is the bare gravitational ADM angular momentum
claims.sourceQuote: We construct smooth axisymmetric electrovacuum exteriors that violate the Kerr--Newman Penrose inequality when \(J\) is the bare gravitational ADM angular momentum and the electromagnetic fields have only \(O(r^{-2})\) decay, allowing angularly varying leading tails.

claims.text: For maximal asymptotically hyperbolic data, mass is bounded below by the Schwarzschild–anti-de Sitter mass of the enclosing area.
claims.sourceLine: the invariant mass is bounded below by the Schwarzschild--anti-de Sitter mass associated with the minimum enclosing area of a weakly future outer-trapped boundary
claims.sourceQuote: Under the dominant energy condition, the stated decay and integrability assumptions, and a future-timelike mass covector, the invariant mass is bounded below by the Schwarzschild--anti-de Sitter mass associated with the minimum enclosing area of a weakly future outer-trapped boundary.

claims.text: Equality identifies the data as a spacelike slice of a Schwarzschild–Tangherlini exterior.
claims.sourceLine: Equality in the spacetime Penrose inequality identifies the original initial data as a spacelike slice of a Schwarzschild--Tangherlini exterior
claims.sourceQuote: Equality in the spacetime Penrose inequality identifies the original initial data as a spacelike slice of a Schwarzschild--Tangherlini exterior, smoothly attached to its horizon, under the stated outermostness and decay hypotheses.
